Ai1.name: Aire 1
Ai1.summary: Aire 1 sits on the upper River Aire downstream of Skipton, draining a catchment of mixed rural pasture and small market towns in the Yorkshire Dales foothills.

Ai2.name: Aire 2
Ai2.summary: Aire 2 is located as the river passes through Leeds, capturing inputs from a large urban and industrial catchment with several wastewater treatment works upstream.

Ai3.name: Aire 3
Ai3.summary: Aire 3 sits downstream of Castleford, draining the lower Aire catchment which combines former coalfield land, arable farmland, and continued urban discharge.

Ca1.name: Calder 1
Ca1.summary: Calder 1 is on the upper River Calder near Halifax, draining steep Pennine valleys with a mix of former textile-mill towns and upland moorland.

Ca2.name: Calder 2
Ca2.summary: Calder 2 sits further downstream near Wakefield, integrating additional urban, industrial, and agricultural inputs from the wider Calder valley.

DwM.name: Derwent M
DwM.summary: Derwent M is a mid-catchment site on the River Derwent, draining a predominantly rural and agricultural landscape in the Vale of Pickering.

DwU.name: Derwent U
DwU.summary: Derwent U is the upper River Derwent site within the North York Moors, characterised by moorland, forestry, and low population density.

Fo1.name: Foss 1
Fo1.summary: Foss 1 is on the upper River Foss north of York, draining low-lying arable land and small villages.

Fo2.name: Foss 2
Fo2.summary: Foss 2 is further downstream as the Foss approaches the outskirts of York, picking up additional urban runoff and agricultural drainage.

Fo3.name: Foss 3
Fo3.summary: Foss 3 sits within York itself, close to the confluence with the River Ouse, integrating the full urban and agricultural catchment above it.

MbSf.name: MeersBrook
MbSf.summary: MeersBrook drains a densely urbanised part of southern Sheffield, with limited green space and significant surface-water and combined-sewer influence.

Ou.name: Ouse
Ou.summary: The Ouse site integrates the combined Aire, Wharfe, Nidd, and Foss catchments as the river flows through York, representing the largest and most mixed upstream catchment in the network.

Rye.name: Rye
Rye.summary: The Rye is a largely rural tributary of the Derwent draining Ryedale, with farmland, small towns, and the Howardian Hills.

Sf.name: Sheaf
Sf.summary: The Sheaf runs through central Sheffield, a heavily urbanised catchment with historic industrial legacy inputs and extensive culverting.

SwU.name: Swale
SwU.summary: Swale is an upland site draining the Yorkshire Dales, with extensive moorland and sheep grazing and very low population density.

WhL.name: Wharfe L
WhL.summary: Wharfe L is a lower-catchment site on the River Wharfe, draining a mix of arable farmland and small settlements before the Wharfe joins the Ouse.

WhM.name: Wharfe M
WhM.summary: Wharfe M sits near Ilkley and Otley, draining a catchment of market towns, pasture, and moorland fringe in mid-Wharfedale.

WhU.name: Wharfe U
WhU.summary: Wharfe U is the upper Wharfedale site above Kettlewell, an upland catchment dominated by moorland and rough grazing with minimal urban influence.

Wi.name: Wiske
Wi.summary: The Wiske drains low-relief arable land in the Vale of Mowbray, with dispersed villages and intensive agriculture as the dominant land use.

GB104027052280.name: Rother from Source to Redleadmill Brook
GB104027052280.summary: This upper Rother catchment is predominantly rural, featuring agricultural land and woodland. Its geology is dominated by Wealden clays and sandstones, influencing drainage. The area experiences a temperate maritime climate with moderate rainfall patterns typical of South East England.

GB104027057290.name: Doe Lea from Source to Hawke Brook
GB104027057290.summary: Located in Derbyshire, this catchment primarily comprises agricultural grazing land and woodland. Geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows a typical East Midlands pattern: moderate annual precipitation with seasonal variations impacting the stream's hydrological response.

GB104027057301.name: Doe Lea from Hawke Brooke to River Rother
GB104027057301.summary: The catchment is characterized by Carboniferous sandstones and shales with a legacy of coal mining. Land use is predominantly agricultural mixed with urban areas. Rainfall follows typical East Midlands patterns, receiving moderate annual precipitation influenced by prevailing westerly winds.

GB104027057310.name: Pools Brook from Source to Doe Lea
GB104027057310.summary: Pools Brook's catchment features predominantly mixed agricultural and pastoral land use. The underlying geology consists mainly of Carboniferous Coal Measures, comprising sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows typical Northern England patterns, with moderate-to-high annual precipitation driving consistent surface runoff.

GB104027057320.name: Hawke Brook from Source to Doe Lea
GB104027057320.summary: The catchment features Carboniferous mudstones and sandstones with land use dominated by agricultural grazing and scattered deciduous woodland. Rainfall patterns are typical for the Pennine fringe of the East Midlands, characterized by moderate to high annual precipitation influencing runoff.

GB104027057340.name: Rivelin from Source to River Loxley
GB104027057340.summary: The Rivelin catchment features upland Millstone Grit geology and acidic soils. Land use transitions from moorland, forestry, and agricultural grazing at the source to urban fringes downstream. It experiences typical Pennine rainfall patterns, characterized by moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027057360.name: Car Brook from Source to River Don
GB104027057360.summary: The catchment comprises predominantly agricultural land and urban fringe areas. Geology is characterized by Carboniferous sandstones and shales with alluvial deposits. Rainfall follows a typical UK temperate maritime pattern, featuring moderate, year-round precipitation influenced by regional topography.

GB104027057370.name: Loxley from Strines Dyke to River Don
GB104027057370.summary: Located in South Yorkshire, this catchment transitions from rural agricultural land to an increasingly urbanized landscape near Sheffield. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous Millstone Grit and Coal Measures, with rainfall patterns typical of Northern England—moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027057380.name: Strines Dyke from Source to River Loxley
GB104027057380.summary: This upland Pennine catchment is characterized by acidic Millstone Grit geology and land use dominated by moorland and rough grazing. Located in the Peak District, it experiences high annual rainfall typical of northern English uplands, driving its hydrological response.

GB104027057390.name: Loxley from Source to Strines Dyke
GB104027057390.summary: Located in the Peak District, this catchment features Millstone Grit geology. Land use transitions from upland moorland and grazing at the source to urbanized areas near Sheffield. Rainfall is high, characteristic of Pennine orography, driving significant seasonal runoff.

GB104027057400.name: Ewden Beck from Source to River Don
GB104027057400.summary: This rural catchment is dominated by agricultural land use, comprising pasture and arable fields. Geologically, it is characterized by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall patterns are typical for Northern England's Pennine foothills, featuring moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027057411.name: Don from Little Don to River Loxley confluence
GB104027057411.summary: This urban South Yorkshire reach is characterized by historical industrial and dense residential land use. The underlying geology consists primarily of Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall patterns are moderate, typical for the region's proximity to the Pennine foothills.

GB104027057412.name: Don from River Loxley confl to  River Don Works
GB104027057412.summary: Located in urban Sheffield, this reach is characterized by high impervious land use. The underlying geology consists primarily of Carboniferous Millstone Grit and Coal Measures. Rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern, significantly influenced by runoff from the adjacent Pennine uplands.

GB104027057413.name: Don from River Don Works to River Rother
GB104027057413.summary: This urbanized South Yorkshire reach features predominantly industrial land use and developed riparian corridors. The geology comprises Carboniferous sandstones and mudstones with fluvial alluvium. Rainfall is moderate to high, following Atlantic-influenced patterns typical of the Northern English midlands.

GB104027057420.name: Greasbrough Dike from Source to River Don
GB104027057420.summary: This catchment features mixed urban, industrial, and agricultural land use typical of the South Yorkshire region. The underlying geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones. It experiences a temperate maritime climate with moderate annual rainfall characteristic of the River Don basin.

GB104027057430.name: Hooton Brook from Source to River Don
GB104027057430.summary: Hooton Brook's catchment is primarily agricultural with scattered woodland and minor urban influences. The geology comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales beneath glacial deposits. It experiences a temperate maritime climate with moderate, year-round rainfall typical of the South Yorkshire region.

GB104027057440.name: Blackburn Brook from Source to River Don
GB104027057440.summary: This catchment features predominantly agricultural land use with increasing urbanisation downstream. It is underlain primarily by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Precipitation follows typical Northern English patterns, with moderate to high annual rainfall influenced by proximity to the Pennine uplands.

GB104027057452.name: Don from River Rother to River Dearne
GB104027057452.summary: Located in South Yorkshire, this reach features heavily urbanized and industrial land use interspersed with agriculture. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and mudstones. It experiences a temperate maritime climate with moderate annual rainfall typical of Northern England.

GB104027057460.name: Little Don from Source to River Don
GB104027057460.summary: The Little Don catchment comprises mixed agricultural grazing and woodland, becoming increasingly urbanized downstream. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows a typical UK maritime pattern, with elevated precipitation occurring in the upland source areas.

GB104027057470.name: Knoll Beck from Source to River Dearne
GB104027057470.summary: Knoll Beck drains a predominantly urbanized South Yorkshire catchment with mixed residential and agricultural land use. The geology features Carboniferous sandstones and shales beneath glacial till deposits, while rainfall follows typical UK temperate maritime patterns of moderate year-round precipitation.

GB104027057480.name: Rockley Dike from Source to River Dove
GB104027057480.summary: This catchment is dominated by agricultural land use, primarily pasture and arable farming. The underlying geology features Triassic sandstones and glacial deposits. Rainfall patterns are typical of the UK Midlands, with moderate precipitation distributed consistently throughout the year.

GB104027057490.name: Don from Scout Dyke to the Little Don
GB104027057490.summary: This waterbody is characterized by a predominantly agricultural landscape focused on grazing and cropping. The underlying geology consists mainly of granites, metamorphic rocks, and glacial deposits. Rainfall follows a typical maritime pattern, with peak precipitation occurring during autumn and winter.

GB104027057500.name: Don from Source to Scout Dyke
GB104027057500.summary: This upland catchment is dominated by moorland and rough grazing on acidic, metamorphic geology. It experiences high annual precipitation typical of the Scottish Highlands, resulting in a flashy hydrological regime influenced by peat-rich soils and rugged mountain terrain.

GB104027057510.name: Dove from Source to River Dearne
GB104027057510.summary: Located in the Pennine uplands, this catchment features a landscape of moorland and grazing pastures. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous limestone and gritstone, creating distinctive karst characteristics. Rainfall is relatively high, heavily influenced by the region's upland topography.

GB104027057520.name: Dodworth Dyke from Source to River Dove
GB104027057520.summary: The catchment is dominated by agricultural land use with localized urban development. Geology primarily comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales. It experiences a temperate maritime climate with moderate, consistent rainfall patterns typical of the South Yorkshire region.

GB104027057530.name: Scout Dyke from Source to River Don
GB104027057530.summary: Located in South Yorkshire, this catchment comprises mixed agricultural and urban land uses. The underlying geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and mudstones. Precipitation follows a typical UK maritime pattern, characterized by moderate rainfall distributed throughout the year.

GB104027057550.name: Ings/Carr/Thurnscoe Dikes from Source to Dearne
GB104027057550.summary: Located in South Yorkshire, this catchment features predominantly agricultural land mixed with urban development. The geology consists of Carboniferous sandstones and shales overlain by glacial till. Rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern, with moderate precipitation distributed throughout the year.

GB104027057560.name: Silkstone Beck from Source to Cawthorne Dyke
GB104027057560.summary: This catchment features mixed agricultural land use—primarily pasture and arable—interspersed with small urban areas. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows a typical UK temperate maritime pattern, with moderate to high annual precipitation across Northern England.

GB104027057600.name: Holme from Source to New Mill Dike
GB104027057600.summary: This upland South Yorkshire catchment is characterized by moorland and pastoral grazing. The geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones and shales. It experiences typical Pennine rainfall patterns, with high annual precipitation occurring primarily during autumn and winter months.

GB104027057610.name: New Mill Dike from Source to River Holme
GB104027057610.summary: Located in the Pennines, this catchment is characterized by Millstone Grit geology and land use dominated by agricultural pasture and upland moorland. It experiences high annual rainfall typical of West Yorkshire’s uplands, heavily influenced by regional orographic precipitation patterns.

GB104027057620.name: Redleadmill Brook
GB104027057620.summary: Redleadmill Brook is situated within a predominantly agricultural catchment featuring upland grazing and moorland. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous limestone and gritstone. Rainfall is high, characteristic of the Peak District's upland environment, with seasonal peaks during winter months.

GB104027057630.name: Rother from Redleadmill Brook to Spital Brook
GB104027057630.summary: This waterbody is situated within a mixed landscape of agriculture and urban development, underlain primarily by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. It experiences typical UK temperate maritime rainfall, characterized by moderate annual precipitation distributed consistently throughout the year.

GB104027057640.name: Spital/Calow/Muster Brook
GB104027057640.summary: This Derbyshire catchment is characterized by predominantly agricultural land use with mixed pasture and arable farming. Geologically, it comprises Carboniferous limestone and gritstone substrates. Rainfall patterns are typical of the region's upland fringes, featuring moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027057660.name: Hipper from Source to River Rother
GB104027057660.summary: The Hipper waterbody flows through a predominantly agricultural landscape of arable farming and grazing land. The underlying geology consists primarily of Jurassic mudstones and sandstones. Rainfall is typical for the East Midlands: moderate, seasonal, and influenced by a temperate maritime climate.

GB104027057670.name: Holme Brook/Linacre Beck
GB104027057670.summary: Holme Brook/Linacre Beck's catchment is characterized by predominantly pastoral land and upland moorland with scattered woodland. The geology comprises Carboniferous Millstone Grit sandstones and shales, while rainfall is relatively high, following the typical orographic patterns of the Pennines.

GB104027057700.name: Barlow Brook from Source to River Drone
GB104027057700.summary: Barlow Brook originates in the Derbyshire uplands, characterized by moorland and agricultural pasture land use. The geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones, which influence soil acidity. Rainfall patterns are typical for the Peak District, featuring high annual precipitation.

GB104027057710.name: Drone/Whitting from Source to River Rother
GB104027057710.summary: This Derbyshire waterbody is characterized by a landscape of agricultural pasture and mixed woodland. The geology primarily comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall is moderate to high, typical of the North Midlands' temperate maritime climate near the Pennine foothills.

GB104027057720.name: The Moss from Source to River Rother
GB104027057720.summary: The Moss catchment is characterized by agricultural pasture and upland moorland. Geology consists primarily of Carboniferous Millstone Grit and mudstones. Rainfall follows typical Pennine-fringe patterns, with higher precipitation in elevated headwaters driving runoff toward the River Rother.

GB104027057730.name: Pigeon Bridge Brook from Source to River Rother
GB104027057730.summary: This catchment is characterized by predominantly agricultural land use with localized urban influences. Geology consists mainly of Carboniferous sandstones and mudstones. Rainfall follows a typical UK temperate maritime pattern, with moderate precipitation distributed relatively evenly throughout the year.

GB104027057740.name: Ulley Brook from Source to River Rother
GB104027057740.summary: This catchment is characterized by predominantly agricultural land use, consisting of pasture and arable farming. The geology comprises sedimentary bedrock and glacial deposits. Rainfall follows a typical UK temperate maritime pattern, with moderate precipitation distributed consistently throughout the year.

GB104027057750.name: Sheaf from Source to River Don
GB104027057750.summary: This catchment transitions from rural uplands and pasture to a dense urban environment. Its geology is primarily Carboniferous Millstone Grit and Triassic sandstones. Rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern, with generally higher precipitation levels occurring in the upstream fringes.

GB104027057760.name: Porter from Source to River Sheaf
GB104027057760.summary: The Porter catchment transitions from upland Millstone Grit moorlands to a heavily urbanized landscape in Sheffield. Geology comprises sandstone and glacial deposits. Rainfall is moderately high, influenced by the orographic effects of the nearby Peak District uplands.

GB104027057771.name: Rother, Spittal Brook to Doe Lea
GB104027057771.summary: This catchment comprises a mix of urban industrial land and agricultural pasture. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales, typical of the Pennine fringe. Rainfall patterns are characteristic of Northern England, featuring moderate to high maritime precipitation.

GB104027057772.name: Rother, Doe Lea to Don
GB104027057772.summary: Located in South Yorkshire, this catchment features mixed land use, combining urban and legacy industrial areas with agricultural pasture. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous Coal Measures, while rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern with moderate precipitation throughout the year.

GB104027057773.name: Shire Brook
GB104027057773.summary: Shire Brook’s catchment is predominantly urban and suburban with mixed agricultural fringes. The geology consists primarily of Mercia Mudstones and Sherwood Sandstone, creating clay-rich soils. Rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern, typical of the UK East Midlands region.

GB104027062510.name: Smithy Brook from Source to River Calder
GB104027062510.summary: Smithy Brook flows through a landscape dominated by Carboniferous Millstone Grit geology. Land use transitions from upland moorland grazing at its source to agricultural and urbanized areas downstream. It experiences high annual precipitation, characteristic of the West Yorkshire Pennine uplands.

GB104027062520.name: Booth Dean Clough from Source to River Ryburn
GB104027062520.summary: This upland waterbody in the Ribble catchment is characterized by rough grazing and moorland land use. The geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones, with high annual rainfall typical of the Pennine uplands influencing its hydrological regime.

GB104027062530.name: Owler Beck from Source to River Calder
GB104027062530.summary: Owler Beck is a heavily urbanized catchment in South Yorkshire, characterized by predominantly residential and industrial land use. The underlying geology comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern with moderate precipitation, influenced by proximity to the Pennines.

GB104027062540.name: Ryburn from Source to Booth Dean Clough
GB104027062540.summary: The Ryburn catchment in the South Pennines is dominated by upland moorland and pastoral grazing. Its geology consists primarily of Millstone Grit sandstones over shales. High annual orographic rainfall characterizes the area, resulting in a typically flashy hydrological response.

GB104027062550.name: Colne from River Holme to River Calder
GB104027062550.summary: This West Yorkshire waterbody features mixed urban, industrial, and agricultural land use. The geology consists primarily of Carboniferous Millstone Grit and shales. The catchment experiences high annual precipitation characteristic of the Pennines, contributing to a relatively flashy hydrological regime.

GB104027062560.name: Oakenshaw Beck from Source to River Calder
GB104027062560.summary: Located in West Yorkshire's Upper Calder catchment, Oakenshaw Beck flows through a mix of urbanized and agricultural land. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous Millstone Grit sandstones, with high annual precipitation patterns characteristic of the Pennine foothills.

GB104027062570.name: Black Brook from Source to River Calder
GB104027062570.summary: Located in the South Pennines, this catchment is characterized by upland moorland and agricultural pasture. The geology primarily comprises Carboniferous Millstone Grit and shales. It experiences high average annual rainfall, typical of the region's maritime temperate climate.

GB104027062580.name: Ryburn from Booth Dean Clough to R Calder
GB104027062580.summary: This Pennine catchment is characterized by upland moorland and pastoral grazing land. The geology consists predominantly of Millstone Grit sandstones and shales, resulting in acidic soils. It experiences high annual orographic rainfall typical of the Northern English highlands.

GB104027062590.name: Choke Churl Bk from Source to River Calder
GB104027062590.summary: Located in West Yorkshire's Pennines, this catchment is characterized by predominantly pastoral land use and woodland. The geology consists primarily of Carboniferous Millstone Grit and shales, supporting high annual rainfall patterns typical of Northern England's upland environments.

GB104027062600.name: Walsden Water from Source to River Calder
GB104027062600.summary: This Pennine upland catchment is characterized by acidic Millstone Grit geology and shales. Land use primarily comprises moorland, rough grazing, and small valley settlements. The area experiences high annual orographic rainfall, resulting in a typically rapid, flashy hydrological response.

GB104027062610.name: Cragg Brook from Source to River Calder
GB104027062610.summary: Cragg Brook is characterized by upland moorland and grazing land within the South Pennines. The geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones. Rainfall is typically high annually, with seasonal peaks during winter, reflecting a characteristic upland West Yorkshire catchment.

GB104027062620.name: Chald from Source to River Calder
GB104027062620.summary: This waterbody is situated within a predominantly agricultural landscape with scattered woodland. The underlying geology consists mainly of Carboniferous sandstones and shales, while rainfall patterns are characteristic of the Pennines, featuring moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027062631.name: Calder from River Colne to River Chald
GB104027062631.summary: This waterbody is situated within a predominantly agricultural landscape characterized by arable farming and grazing. The underlying geology consists primarily of Chalk and glacial deposits, while rainfall follows typical southeastern England patterns with moderate annual precipitation and seasonal variability.

GB104027062632.name: Calder from River Chald to River Aire
GB104027062632.summary: Located in West Yorkshire, this catchment transitions from upland moorland grazing to intensive urban and industrial land use. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales, while high Pennine rainfall patterns result in a characteristically flashy hydrological regime.

GB104027062641.name: Calder from Colden Water to Ryburn Confluence
GB104027062641.summary: This South Pennine catchment is characterized by upland moorland and rough grazing. Geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones and shales, resulting in typically acidic soils. The area receives high annual rainfall characteristic of an Atlantic-influenced upland climate.

GB104027062642.name: Calder from Ryburn Confluence  to River Colne
GB104027062642.summary: Located in the Pennines, this catchment features a landscape of upland moorland and lowland agricultural land. Geology is primarily Carboniferous Millstone Grit and shale. The area experiences high annual rainfall with characteristic orographic effects typical of Northern England.

GB104027062650.name: Calder from Walsden Water to Colden Water
GB104027062650.summary: Located in the Pennines, this waterbody is characterized by upland moorland and livestock grazing. The geology primarily comprises Carboniferous Millstone Grit and shales. It experiences high orographic rainfall, typical of the West Yorkshire and Lancashire upland environments.

GB104027062660.name: Calder from Source to Walsden Water
GB104027062660.summary: This upland Pennine catchment features predominantly moorland and pastoral grazing land. The geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones and shales. It experiences high annual rainfall typical of the region's orographic pattern, resulting in a characteristically rapid hydrological response.

GB104027062670.name: Batley Beck from Source to River Calder
GB104027062670.summary: This urbanized West Yorkshire catchment is dominated by industrial and residential land use alongside small agricultural areas. Its geology comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales, while rainfall follows typical Pennine patterns—moderate to high with seasonal winter peaks.

GB104027062680.name: Oulton Beck from Source to River Aire
GB104027062680.summary: Oulton Beck flows through a predominantly urbanized and agricultural landscape in West Yorkshire. The underlying geology comprises mainly Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Rainfall follows typical northern English patterns, characterized by moderate to high annual precipitation influenced by a maritime climate.

GB104027062690.name: Colden Water from Source to River Calder
GB104027062690.summary: Located in West Yorkshire, this catchment features upland moorlands and agricultural pastures. The geology is dominated by Carboniferous Millstone Grit sandstones. It experiences high annual rainfall typical of the South Pennines, which drives significant runoff into the River Calder.

GB104027062700.name: Clifton Beck from Source to River Calder
GB104027062700.summary: Clifton Beck flows through West Yorkshire's mixed agricultural and urban landscapes. The catchment is dominated by Millstone Grit and shales. Rainfall patterns are moderately high, characteristic of the Pennine foothills, influencing the hydrological response within this upland-influenced system.

GB104027062710.name: Spen Beck from Source to River Calder
GB104027062710.summary: Spen Beck drains a West Yorkshire catchment characterized by Carboniferous sandstones and shales. Land use is predominantly urban and industrial, interspersed with agricultural pasture. It experiences high annual rainfall typical of northern England's maritime climate, heavily influenced by the Pennines.

GB104027062720.name: Red Beck, Source to Calder and Hebble Navigation
GB104027062720.summary: Red Beck is situated in a predominantly agricultural landscape featuring upland grazing and moorland. The geology consists mainly of Millstone Grit sandstones. It experiences high annual rainfall characteristic of the Pennines, resulting in a flashy hydrological response before joining the Calder.

GB104027062731.name: Hebden Water from Widdop Beck to R Calder
GB104027062731.summary: This Pennine catchment is characterized by Millstone Grit geology and acidic, peaty soils. Land use transitions from upland moorland and grazing in the headwaters to pastoral farming and small urban settlements downstream, with high annual rainfall typical of West Yorkshire.

GB104027062740.name: The Fleet from Source to River Aire
GB104027062740.summary: This West Yorkshire catchment features a mosaic of urban development and agricultural land. Geologically dominated by Carboniferous sandstones and shales (Millstone Grit), it experiences temperate maritime rainfall patterns typical of Northern England, with seasonal precipitation peaks in autumn and winter.

GB104027062750.name: Milshaw Beck from Source to Low/Wortley/Pudsey Bks
GB104027062750.summary: Located in West Yorkshire, this predominantly urbanized catchment features residential and commercial land use with small agricultural fringes. The geology primarily comprises Carboniferous sandstones and shales, while rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern typical of Northern England.

GB104027062770.name: Luddenden Brook from Source to River Calder
GB104027062770.summary: Luddenden Brook drains a predominantly Millstone Grit catchment in the South Pennines. Land use transitions from upland moorland and grazing to valley-bottom urban settlements. The area experiences high annual rainfall characteristic of the region's orographic patterns, significantly influencing its hydrology.

GB104027062780.name: Hebble Brook from Source to River Calder
GB104027062780.summary: This West Yorkshire catchment features a landscape transitioning from upland grazing and forestry to lowland agriculture and urban areas. Geology is dominated by Millstone Grit sandstones and shales, while high annual rainfall is characteristic of its position in the South Pennines.

GB104027062810.name: Lin Dike from Source to River Aire
GB104027062810.summary: The Lin Dike catchment in West Yorkshire is characterized by primarily agricultural land use with interspersed woodland. It is underlain by Carboniferous sandstones and shales, receiving moderate to high annual rainfall patterns typical of the northern Pennine foothills.

GB104027062820.name: Crimsworth Dean Beck from Source to Hebden Water
GB104027062820.summary: This upland catchment in the South Pennines is dominated by rough grazing and moorland. The geology consists primarily of Millstone Grit, while the area experiences high annual rainfall typical of the region's hilly terrain, draining into Hebden Water.

GB104027062830.name: Low/Wortley/Pudsey Bks
GB104027062830.summary: Located in an urbanised area of West Yorkshire, this catchment is characterised by predominantly residential and industrial land use. The geology consists primarily of Carboniferous sandstones and shales, while rainfall follows a temperate maritime pattern with moderate to high annual precipitation.

GB104027062840.name: Graining Water from Widdop Resr to Hebden Wat
GB104027062840.summary: Located in the South Pennines, this catchment is characterized by upland moorland and rough grazing land use. The geology consists primarily of Millstone Grit sandstones and shales, experiencing high annual rainfall typical of an orographic uplift upland environment.

GB104027062850.name: Alcomden Water - Walshaw Dean Resrs to Widdop
GB104027062850.summary: This upland Pennine catchment is characterized by Millstone Grit geology and acidic peat soils. Land use is dominated by moorland grazing and forestry. The area experiences high annual rainfall, resulting in rapid runoff typical of high-altitude, low-permeability terrains.

GB104027062861.name: Clayton Beck (Source to Bradford Bk)
